text:
jamie: Seeing a weird pattern — apiserver 502s only during large GPU pool scaleups in east-us-2. Control plane FD counts spike and some controller-manager reconciles stall. Anyone else seeing this?

sasha: Yep saw it start ~2026-03-22T03:12Z during a bulk attach burst. apiserver logs include "accept: too many open files" and a bunch of proxy resets.

linda: Can you paste the exact journal lines and the autoscaler concurrency during the window? Also, any etcd compaction activity?

jamie: Logs pasted below (redacted):
```
Mar 22 03:12:15 kube-apiserver[1]: E03 2026-03-22 03:12:15 server.go:123] dial tcp 10.10.1.5:2379: connect: connection refused
Mar 22 03:12:16 kube-apiserver[1]: E03 2026-03-22 03:12:16 server.go:456] accept unix /var/run/proxy.sock: too many open files
Mar 22 03:12:16 kube-apiserver[1]: W03 2026-03-22 03:12:16 handler.go:78] proxy reset for clientID=svc-gpu-provisioner
```

sasha: NVMe iops and avgqu-sz spiked on controlplane nodes in the same 60s window. etcd leader moved 3x in 2m which amplified connection churn.

raul: The GPU provisioning flow does bursty node attach ops (we have a hot path that attaches ~150 nodes over ~45s). That generates a ton of kubelet health probes and new watch connections; kube-apiserver proxy pools can exhaust FDs under that pattern. We should rate-limit attach concurrency.

linda: Do we have numbers for current FD usage on the apiserver pods? Also controller-manager logs — are reconciles blocked waiting on API calls?

jamie: Quick snapshot from the canary node: `lsof -p <apiserver-pid> | wc -l` returned ~62k during peak. controller-manager showed many backoff events: "Get /api/v1/nodes: context deadline exceeded"

oncall-bot: runbook triggered: controlplane-fd-surge. Checks queued: fd-check, etcd-health, nvme-iops. Incident ID: INC-3250004321.

sasha: Immediate mitigations: 1) temp increase systemd LimitNOFILE for kube-apiserver to 65536, 2) throttle autoscaler surge for the GPU pool to reduce attach concurrency, 3) add short stagger to attach process. Rolling the ulimit now.

raul: Long term: change attach to staggered attach with jitter, implement backoff on the provisioner to avoid synchronous LB and kubelet flurries, and consider reducing watch fanout via a small kube-apiserver cache tuning (shorter watch keepalive for ephemeral probes).

linda: Also worth looking at etcd compaction timing — if compaction coincides with attach bursts it may compound IO pressure. Can ops schedule compactions outside of heavy scaling windows?

jamie: I reduced the autoscaler max surge from 200 -> 20 for the GPU pool and kicked a canary. Monitoring apiserver 5xx rate, etcd leader stability, and NVMe queue length.

sasha: I'll follow up with a permanent systemd change and a dashboard to alert on apiserver FD usage and avgqu-sz.

raul: I'll draft a patch for the provisioner to add concurrency limits and jitter. Will post PR link in this thread.

linda: Action items: sasha => persist ulimit and dashboard, raul => provisioner backoff PR, jamie => validate SLO impact and revert surge if needed. :white_check_mark:

jamie: Thanks — posting metrics in ~10m and will update when canary finishes.
